Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO on November 23, 11 days after he resigned.
The board said U.S. officials gave input and it found no national security risk. Its independent investigation continues.
Gizmodo reported the stock jumped nearly 30%.

Was bringing him back the right call?

paragraphs.text: Nvidia's board of directors voted unanimously on November 23, 2026 to reinstate Jensen Huang as the company's president, chief executive officer and a member of the board, effective immediately, according to a company press release filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

The decision reverses Huang's resignation on November 12, according to TheWrap. Gizmodo reported that Nvidia shares jumped nearly 30% after the announcement, a sharp move for a company that had lost hundreds of billions of dollars in market value during the weeks of turmoil around his exit.

TheWrap reported that Huang stepped down after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with a businesswoman whom U.S. intelligence officials suspected of having ties to Chinese intelligence services. He also faced scrutiny over relationships with Nvidia employees, the outlet reported. Gizmodo described the episode as a spy scandal and reported that Huang later admitted to the affair.

The reversal came quickly. According to TheWrap, board chairman Harvey Jones told investors the previous Tuesday that the company had no intention of bringing its co-founder back. Huang said that same day that he would be honored to return if the board decided it was in the company's best interest, the outlet reported.

In its release, Nvidia said the board held a series of discussions and meetings with Huang and was satisfied with his candor and his ability to lead the company. The board also said it received input from senior levels of the U.S. government and concluded that the reinstatement poses no national security risk. Jones said in the release that the board believes Huang is the right person to lead Nvidia, and he remains chairman.

Colette Kress, who led the company as interim CEO while also serving as chief financial officer, returns to her role as CFO, the company said. Nvidia thanked her for her service as interim chief executive.

Political pressure for the move had been public. Gizmodo reported that President Donald Trump praised the decision on Truth Social shortly after the announcement, after saying at a November 20 news conference that the company should accept an apology and let Huang go back to work.

The reinstatement does not end the inquiry into Huang's conduct. Nvidia said a committee made up only of independent directors, advised by independent counsel, will continue investigating reports that Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort, and that the review will proceed to its conclusion. Huang said he fully supports the investigation and will cooperate, according to the release.

The company also announced new oversight. The board created a National Security and Export Control Committee of independent directors to oversee trade compliance and national security risks, and Nvidia is searching for a chief compliance officer who will report to the board's nominating and corporate governance committee. Nvidia said it will keep cooperating with ongoing government investigations and inquiries.

The speed of the reversal shows how closely investors tie Nvidia's value to its founder. In NeuraFeed's reading, the board chose to bet that new compliance structures and government assurances can contain the risk of his return, rather than run the world's most important AI chip supplier without him while a CEO search dragged on. That bet now rests on an investigation whose findings are still unknown.

The next marker is the independent committee's report on the foreign intelligence allegations, along with the name of Nvidia's first chief compliance officer, both of which will show whether the board's conditions on Huang's return carry real weight.
